title: Select columns and aliases
summary: Select only the columns needed by the caller.
syntax:
SELECT expression AS output_name, other_column
FROM table_name AS alias;
rules: Select only the columns needed by the caller.
AS names an output column or table alias; double quotes delimit identifiers, single quotes delimit text.
Shared examples verified on SQLite 3.53.1 and PostgreSQL 18.4.

title: Filter rows
summary: WHERE retains only rows where the predicate is true; unknown is excluded.
syntax:
SELECT columns FROM source
WHERE predicate AND (other_predicate OR fallback);
rules: WHERE retains only rows where the predicate is true; unknown is excluded.
Use parentheses to make AND/OR grouping clear; BETWEEN includes both endpoints.
Shared examples verified on SQLite 3.53.1 and PostgreSQL 18.4.

title: Order and limit
summary: Without ORDER BY, row order is unspecified.
rules: Without ORDER BY, row order is unspecified.
Break ties with a unique key. NULL ordering differs by engine; use NULLS FIRST/LAST explicitly.
Shared examples verified on SQLite 3.53.1 and PostgreSQL 18.4.

title: Join related tables
summary: INNER JOIN emits matching pairs; one customer can produce multiple order rows.
rules: INNER JOIN emits matching pairs; one customer can produce multiple order rows.
Qualify shared column names with table aliases and put the relationship in ON.
Shared examples verified on SQLite 3.53.1 and PostgreSQL 18.4.

title: Find missing relationships
summary: LEFT JOIN preserves the left row and fills missing right columns with NULL.
syntax:
SELECT a.columns
FROM parent AS a
LEFT JOIN child AS b ON b.parent_id = a.id
WHERE b.id IS NULL;
rules: LEFT JOIN preserves the left row and fills missing right columns with NULL.
Test a non-nullable right-side key; a right-side filter in WHERE can accidentally remove unmatched parents.
Shared examples verified on SQLite 3.53.1 and PostgreSQL 18.4.

title: Group totals and filter groups
summary: WHERE filters input rows; HAVING filters aggregated groups.
syntax:
SELECT grouping_key, SUM(amount) AS total
FROM source
GROUP BY grouping_key
HAVING SUM(amount) > threshold;
rules: WHERE filters input rows; HAVING filters aggregated groups.
Group every selected non-aggregate column for portable results. COUNT(*) counts rows; COUNT(column) skips NULL.
Shared examples verified on SQLite 3.53.1 and PostgreSQL 18.4.

title: NULL and three-valued logic
summary: Use IS NULL or IS NOT NULL; comparisons to NULL evaluate to unknown.
rules: Use IS NULL or IS NOT NULL; comparisons to NULL evaluate to unknown.
WHERE keeps true only. NOT unknown remains unknown; use NOT EXISTS instead of NOT IN when the set can contain NULL.
Shared examples verified on SQLite 3.53.1 and PostgreSQL 18.4.

title: Subqueries and EXISTS
summary: EXISTS checks whether the subquery returns at least one row.
syntax:
SELECT p.columns FROM parent AS p
WHERE EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM child AS c WHERE c.parent_id = p.id);
rules: EXISTS checks whether the subquery returns at least one row.
A correlated subquery references the outer row; NOT EXISTS safely handles nullable inner columns.
Shared examples verified on SQLite 3.53.1 and PostgreSQL 18.4.

title: Common table expressions
summary: A CTE names a result within one statement; it is not a persistent table.
syntax:
WITH named_result AS (SELECT columns FROM source)
SELECT columns FROM named_result;
rules: A CTE names a result within one statement; it is not a persistent table.
Do not assume a CTE forces materialization or improves performance.
Shared examples verified on SQLite 3.53.1 and PostgreSQL 18.4.

title: Window functions
summary: Window functions retain individual rows; GROUP BY collapses them.
rules: Window functions retain individual rows; GROUP BY collapses them.
ROW_NUMBER breaks ties using ORDER BY; RANK leaves gaps, DENSE_RANK does not. Use an explicit ROWS frame for running sums.
Shared examples verified on SQLite 3.53.1 and PostgreSQL 18.4.

title: Insert rows
summary: List target columns explicitly; omitted columns use defaults or NULL when allowed.
syntax:
INSERT INTO table_name (column_a, column_b)
VALUES (value_a, value_b);
rules: List target columns explicitly; omitted columns use defaults or NULL when allowed.
A failed constraint rejects the statement; client code must still manage the surrounding transaction.
Shared examples verified on SQLite 3.53.1 and PostgreSQL 18.4.

title: Update selected rows
summary: Omitting WHERE changes every row.
syntax: UPDATE table_name SET column = expression WHERE predicate;
rules: Omitting WHERE changes every row.
Inspect the predicate with SELECT and check the affected row count in your client.
Shared examples verified on SQLite 3.53.1 and PostgreSQL 18.4.

title: Delete selected rows
summary: Omitting WHERE deletes every row.
syntax: DELETE FROM table_name WHERE predicate;
rules: Omitting WHERE deletes every row.
Foreign keys can reject a deletion; explicit transactions let you inspect changes before committing.
Shared examples verified on SQLite 3.53.1 and PostgreSQL 18.4.

title: Keys and constraints
summary: PRIMARY KEY identifies rows; NOT NULL, UNIQUE, CHECK and foreign keys protect data invariants.
syntax:
CREATE TABLE table_name (
  id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY,
  name TEXT NOT NULL,
  code TEXT UNIQUE,
  amount INTEGER CHECK (amount >= 0),
  parent_id INTEGER REFERENCES parent(id)
);
rules: PRIMARY KEY identifies rows; NOT NULL, UNIQUE, CHECK and foreign keys protect data invariants.
SQLite foreign-key enforcement must be enabled on every connection; PostgreSQL enables it automatically. CHECK permits unknown, so add NOT NULL where needed.
Shared examples verified on SQLite 3.53.1 and PostgreSQL 18.4.

title: Indexes and query plans
summary: Indexes can speed reads but add storage and write cost.
rules: Indexes can speed reads but add storage and write cost.
Column order matters in composite indexes; inspect real plans rather than assuming an index will be used.
Shared examples verified on SQLite 3.53.1 and PostgreSQL 18.4.

title: Transactions and rollback
summary: COMMIT keeps changes; ROLLBACK discards uncommitted changes. Use the same connection throughout.
rules: COMMIT keeps changes; ROLLBACK discards uncommitted changes. Use the same connection throughout.
After an error PostgreSQL aborts the transaction until rollback (or rollback to an earlier savepoint); SQLite often aborts only the statement. Clients must explicitly recover.
Shared examples verified on SQLite 3.53.1 and PostgreSQL 18.4.

title: Bound parameters
summary: Placeholders bind values, not table/column names. Pass parameters through the client API, never interpolate them into SQL.
rules: Placeholders bind values, not table/column names. Pass parameters through the client API, never interpolate them into SQL.
SQLite Python uses ? or :name; node-postgres and Go pgx use $1. A plain SQL console does not automatically bind these markers.
Shared examples verified on SQLite 3.53.1 and PostgreSQL 18.4.

title: SQLite connection setup
summary: Enable foreign keys before opening a transaction on every SQLite connection.
rules: Enable foreign keys before opening a transaction on every SQLite connection.
Use exactly INTEGER PRIMARY KEY for a rowid alias. PostgreSQL uses identity columns instead.
Supported fixture: SQLite 3.53.1.

title: PostgreSQL identity and RETURNING
summary: PostgreSQL identity generates a value from a sequence; a primary key also enforces uniqueness.
rules: PostgreSQL identity generates a value from a sequence; a primary key also enforces uniqueness.
RETURNING yields changed rows; sequence values may have gaps after rollback.
Supported fixture: PostgreSQL 18.4.

title: PostgreSQL upsert
summary: The conflict target needs a unique or exclusion constraint supported by the selected action.
syntax:
-- PostgreSQL only
INSERT INTO table_name (key, value) VALUES ($1, $2)
ON CONFLICT (key) DO UPDATE SET value = EXCLUDED.value
RETURNING key, value;
rules: The conflict target needs a unique or exclusion constraint supported by the selected action.
EXCLUDED contains the proposed row. This card documents PostgreSQL behavior even though SQLite has related syntax.
Supported fixture: PostgreSQL 18.4.

title: PostgreSQL JSONB
summary: JSONB stores parsed JSON; ->> extracts a JSON property as SQL text.
rules: JSONB stores parsed JSON; ->> extracts a JSON property as SQL text.
JSON null, missing keys and SQL NULL differ; PostgreSQL casts/operators do not transfer directly to SQLite JSON functions.
Supported fixture: PostgreSQL 18.4.

title: Distinct rows and duplicate semantics
summary: DISTINCT deduplicates the complete projected row; COUNT(DISTINCT x) excludes NULL.
syntax:
SELECT DISTINCT column FROM source;
SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT column) FROM source;
rules: Multiple NULLs form one DISTINCT result; adding another output column changes the deduplication key.
Use ORDER BY for stable presentation; DISTINCT does not select a representative whole record.
Verified on SQLite 3.53.1 and PostgreSQL 18.4.

title: Combine, intersect and subtract relations
summary: UNION removes duplicates; UNION ALL preserves them. INTERSECT keeps common rows; EXCEPT subtracts rows.
rules: Each arm must project the same number of compatible columns; sort the final relation.
NULLs compare equal for set deduplication. Parenthesize mixed operations with derived tables: precedence differs by engine.
Verified on SQLite 3.53.1 and PostgreSQL 18.4.

title: Conditional projections and safe missing values
summary: CASE chooses a branch; COALESCE selects the first non-NULL value; NULLIF turns a matching value into NULL.
syntax:
CASE WHEN predicate THEN value ELSE fallback END
COALESCE(nullable_value, fallback)
amount * 1.0 / NULLIF(denominator, 0)
rules: An omitted ELSE yields NULL. Empty text and zero are values, not NULL.
Use NULLIF to guard zero denominators; cast deliberately to avoid integer division. Do not rely on CASE hiding constant planner errors.
Verified on SQLite 3.53.1 and PostgreSQL 18.4.

title: Self joins and one-to-many cardinality
summary: A join emits matching pairs; joining two one-to-many relations can multiply quantities.
syntax:
SELECT child.id, parent.name FROM employees child
LEFT JOIN employees parent ON parent.id = child.manager_id;
rules: Aggregate child data before joining to avoid double-counting. DISTINCT totals cannot repair duplicated amounts.
Self joins require separate aliases. Filter an optional right relation in ON to preserve unmatched left rows.
Verified on SQLite 3.53.1 and PostgreSQL 18.4.

title: Stable keyset and offset pagination
summary: A unique tie-breaker makes pages deterministic for an unchanged dataset.
rules: The continuation predicate must match every ORDER BY direction; nullable sort keys need a separate policy.
OFFSET can skip/repeat rows under concurrent insertion. Keysets do not freeze the dataset; use a snapshot when required.
Verified on SQLite 3.53.1 and PostgreSQL 18.4.

title: Filtered aggregates and group boundaries
summary: FILTER chooses rows per aggregate; HAVING chooses whole groups.
syntax:
SELECT key, COUNT(*) FILTER (WHERE predicate)
FROM source GROUP BY key HAVING COUNT(*) >= minimum;
rules: COUNT returns zero for an empty input; SUM returns NULL, so COALESCE totals when zero is the domain default.
After LEFT JOIN, count the non-null child key rather than COUNT(*) when counting children.
Verified on SQLite 3.53.1 and PostgreSQL 18.4.

title: Window ties and explicit frames
summary: RANGE CURRENT ROW includes ordering peers; ROWS counts individual ordered rows.
syntax:
SUM(value) OVER (ORDER BY value RANGE BETWEEN UNBOUNDED PRECEDING AND CURRENT ROW)
SUM(value) OVER (ORDER BY value, id ROWS BETWEEN 1 PRECEDING AND CURRENT ROW)
rules: RANK leaves gaps after ties; DENSE_RANK does not. ROW_NUMBER needs a unique tie-breaker for stable assignments.
LAST_VALUE uses the current frame, not necessarily the partition end. Specify UNBOUNDED FOLLOWING for the final partition value.
Verified on SQLite 3.53.1 and PostgreSQL 18.4.

title: Bounded recursive traversal
summary: A recursive CTE combines an anchor and a recursive term until no new rows remain.
rules: Use a finite depth bound for potentially cyclic hierarchies; an outer LIMIT is not a portable recursion safety guard.
UNION deduplicates full rows, so adding depth can prevent cycle elimination. Order output explicitly; traversal order is not presentation order.
Verified on SQLite 3.53.1 and PostgreSQL 18.4.

title: Transactional additive schema changes
summary: Additive migrations can preserve existing rows with an explicit compatible default.
rules: A failed PostgreSQL transaction needs rollback; SQLite statement failure can leave the transaction active. Test recovery on the same connection.
Do not claim arbitrary ALTER forms are portable. Table rebuilds require preserving indexes, triggers and foreign keys; this unit limits itself to additive columns and rename.
Verified on SQLite 3.53.1 and PostgreSQL 18.4.

title: Recover optional work within a transaction
summary: A savepoint lets a caller undo a portion of a transaction without discarding earlier work.
rules: ROLLBACK TO keeps the savepoint; RELEASE removes it. Releasing an inner savepoint does not commit the outer transaction.
Place a savepoint before work that can fail. PostgreSQL rejects further statements after an error until rollback; recover before continuing.
Verified on SQLite 3.53.1 and PostgreSQL 18.4.

title: SQLite conflict-targeted imports
summary: SQLite UPSERT handles a named uniqueness conflict without hiding other integrity failures.
syntax:
INSERT INTO source (key, value) VALUES (?, ?)
ON CONFLICT (key) DO UPDATE SET value = excluded.value;
rules: DO NOTHING leaves the existing row. Target a declared unique key. NOT NULL, CHECK and foreign-key failures remain errors.
Avoid INSERT OR REPLACE for updates: replacement can delete/reinsert a row and trigger foreign-key effects. These examples use SQLite 3.53.1.
Verified on SQLite 3.53.1.

title: SQLite writer locking and optimistic guards
summary: BEGIN IMMEDIATE acquires the writer reservation before read-modify-write work. SQLite allows one writer at a time.
rules: Use bounded busy handling and retry the whole transaction after rollback; a deferred read snapshot cannot always upgrade to a writer.
WAL permits readers during writes; it does not permit multiple writers. Check affected rows for optimistic old-value predicates.
Verified on SQLite 3.53.1.

title: PostgreSQL snapshots and concurrent updates
summary: Read Committed uses a fresh snapshot per statement; Repeatable Read retains a snapshot from the first data statement.
rules: UPDATE value = value + delta avoids a stale client-side overwrite but does not enforce cross-row business invariants.
Repeatable Read and Serializable can reject concurrent updates with 40001. Roll back and retry the whole transaction, with a bounded retry policy.
Verified on PostgreSQL 18.4.

title: SQLite JSON validity and missing keys
summary: SQLite JSON functions operate on JSON text; validate malformed text before extraction.
syntax:
CASE WHEN json_valid(payload) THEN json_extract(payload, '$.key') END
json_type(payload, '$.key')
rules: json_extract returns SQL NULL for a missing key and JSON null; json_type distinguishes missing (SQL NULL) from JSON null (text null).
Guard extraction with CASE. This is SQLite JSON syntax, not PostgreSQL JSONB casting or containment.
Verified on SQLite 3.53.1.

title: SQLite UTC timestamps and invalid inputs
summary: Normalize known ISO-8601 offsets with SQLite date functions; keep range bounds half-open.
syntax:
datetime(iso_text)
strftime('%Y-%m-%d', iso_text)
WHERE utc_text >= lower_bound AND utc_text < upper_bound
rules: SQLite has no dedicated timestamp storage type. Store a consistent UTC representation before comparing text lexically.
Invalid inputs can yield NULL; date normalization is not a full domain validator. Use fixed inputs for deterministic checks, not now or host localtime.
Verified on SQLite 3.53.1.

title: PostgreSQL instants and reporting zones
summary: TIMESTAMPTZ represents an instant; its display depends on the session time zone.
syntax:
instant::timestamptz AT TIME ZONE 'UTC'
WHERE instant >= lower_bound::timestamptz AND instant < upper_bound::timestamptz
rules: Specify offsets when ingesting text and explicit report zones for calendar grouping. TIMESTAMP WITHOUT TIME ZONE has no instant until interpreted in a zone.
Malformed casts fail; reject or validate input at the boundary. Prefer half-open intervals and fixed instants; DST days need not be 24 hours.
Verified on PostgreSQL 18.4.
